memory_lessons.applicability: For this same two-pass hierarchy and 128-thread CTA reduction, an intermediate tile tests the observed non-monotonic tile-size tradeoff while holding other code constant.
memory_lessons.claim: The 4096-tile candidate was valid at 7.3306 μs versus 8.0365 μs for the 2048-tile candidate, while the 8192-tile candidate was valid but slower at 17.6395 μs. This supports testing an intermediate tile, not assuming larger tiles are faster.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 3072-tile candidate for correctness and repeated full-program timings; compare it with the 4096-tile parent and supplied baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: An intermediate 3072-element tile may balance first-pass CTA parallelism against partial/finalizer work better than either measured 2048/4096 tiles or the much slower 8192 tile. For large inputs it generates more CTAs and partials than 4096, but fewer than 2048; the experiment tests that tradeoff without assuming fewer launches or partials alone predict speed.

retained: Change the tile size from 4096 to 3072, extending the one-CTA path through 3072 elements and setting the large-input partial count to ceil(n/3072).

Retain the 128-thread shared-memory CTA reduction, 64-bit intermediate sums, bounded tail handling, initialized-per-call partial writes, two-pass finalization, n=0 empty sum, ABI, and default-stream behavior.
